identification.name: AISI 1018 Steel (Cold-Drawn)
identification.common_form_notes: Most commonly stocked as cold-drawn round bar (the default form for machined shafts, pins, and general stock); also available hot-rolled in sheet and plate. Excellent machinability makes it a common general-purpose choice when high strength isn't required.
identification.notes: Low-carbon (~0.18% C) steel, cold-drawn condition — mechanical properties are specific to cold-drawn bar stock and are noticeably higher than the hot-rolled condition of the same grade. Thermal properties (CTE, thermal conductivity, specific heat) are reported for the annealed condition since cold-drawn-specific thermal data wasn't found; these properties don't vary meaningfully with cold work for plain carbon steels. Young's modulus: AZoM and MatWeb sources both point to ~205 GPa (MatWeb's page literally states "0.205 GPa", an evident source typo for 205 GPa); TheWorldMaterial separately lists 186 GPa for the grade generally (not tied to a specific condition) — used 205 GPa as the representative value given two-source agreement. MatWeb's page also has an evident order-of-magnitude typo for Tensile Strength Ultimate ("440000 MPa") and Shear Modulus ("0.0800 GPa") — both disregarded in favor of AZoM/TheWorldMaterial agreement (440 MPa tensile) and the standard isotropic relation (shear modulus not stored; derived.js computes G = E/(2(1+ν)) ≈ 79.5 GPa from the stored E and ν, consistent with AZoM's directly stated 80.0 GPa). Shear strength derived from von Mises criterion: UTS/√3 = 440/1.732 ≈ 254 MPa. Electrical conductivity derived from MatWeb's stated resistivity (1.59×10⁻⁵ Ω·cm @ 0°C) via %IACS = (1.7241 µΩ·cm / 15.9 µΩ·cm) × 100 ≈ 10.8% IACS.

typical_usage: General-purpose machined parts, shafts, pins, dowels, spacers, mounting plates, fixtures, and carburized components (gears, worms, ratchets) where high surface hardness with a tough core is wanted. Not for high-strength or high-fatigue applications — use 4340 or a spring steel instead. The default "just need a steel part" choice for capstone machining.
